scope: Source-first manual semantic inventory frozen after full body reading and before cohort-specific current-field comparison. Prior project sources and corpus context are known; this is not blind or independent acceptance. Scientific propositions, fictional premises and production contracts are distinct.

requirements.requirement: In the fictional oriented main specimen invasive cancer reaches the original lateral ink; the additional specimen has a distinct old-facing surface and new final outer ink, related to the main specimen by the stipulated orientation.
Invasive cancer also reaches the additional specimen new final outer ink in this toy case; the old main edge does not alone decide the final margin.
A separate 0.7 mm DCIS-to-evaluated-ink inset is narrow negative, not at ink. The invented measurement does not independently determine adequacy or an operation.

The fictional examples assume complete resected breast and all sampled regional nodes after neoadjuvant systemic therapy, retaining explicit protocol-specific nodal rules and no inference about unsampled tissue.
No invasive breast disease, residual DCIS and no invasive sampled-node disease meets ypT0/Tis ypN0 but fails the stricter ypT0 ypN0 definition.
The otherwise matching example with a 4 mm invasive regional-node deposit fails both pCR definitions; the deposit does not assign an overall stage.

DCIS at the evaluated final ink remains a margin question in both examples; satisfying one response definition does not settle the margin, prove cure, whole-body absence or trial-level survival benefit.

RCB separates breast-bed footprint dimensions, cancer-area cellularity and the in-situ share of cancer, plus involved regional-node count and largest metastasis size; these are not interchangeable denominators.
The brief is protocol-specific RCB teaching, excludes neoadjuvant endocrine therapy, and gives no calculator result, patient recurrence percentage or sequencing-purity estimate.

Gross fibrous bed, the largest contiguous residual invasive focus for ypT, and two-dimensional residual RCB extent have different purposes; neither fibrous extent nor one invasive focus substitutes for every measurement.
Residual-bed cellularity needs its own evaluated-area denominator; the same invented scattered foci can yield different valid extent measurements.
Fibrosis alone establishes neither drug-specific response nor absence of cancer; pathological viable appearance is not a culture viability assay. The drawing assigns no individual stage or score.
The invented 5 by 4 equal-area grid has 20 tiles across 100 bed-area units, each tile 5 units; 1 tile is in situ, 3 invasive and 16 other evaluated bed area.
Four cancer tiles yield 20 of 100 bed-area units, 20% overall cancer cellularity; the remaining 80% is other bed area, not necessarily all scar or all normal cells.
Repeating only the four cancer tiles changes the denominator: in situ is 1/4=25% and invasive is 3/4=75% of cancer area, with no progression or conversion implied.
The fictional invasive whole-bed share is 20% times 75%=15%, and in-situ whole-bed share is 5%; the denominators and units remain explicit.

The tile arithmetic illustrates area fractions, not nuclei or cell counts, a prescribed pixel-counting pathology workflow, exact precision, a clinical cutoff, sequencing purity, RCB category or a personal forecast.

Different drugs and perioperative blocks can belong to one early-setting strategy; a later first metastatic systemic strategy retains earlier exposure history but does not automatically become a later metastatic line.

The fictional strategy schematic supplies no universal maintenance, pause or switch rule and no survival prediction; clinical setting and prior exposure remain separate from metastatic-line numbering.
A predefined combined response rule is met only when every required interpretable assessment meets its condition; the example requires an MRI criterion and an adequate negative biopsy.
MRI criterion met plus inadequate biopsy cannot qualify the branch: an inadequate specimen is neither a negative test nor proof of positive residual disease.
Response prediction is distinct from measured surgical pCR; rule-based branching alone proves neither long-term benefit nor equivalence and supplies no treatment-omission instruction.
I-SPY 2.2 and CREATE-X have different trial populations, designs and evidentiary jobs; a cited trial and an author source-reading attestation do not verify the fictional rule or component benefit.

The historical KEYNOTE-522-type stage II-III TNBC strategy comprises paclitaxel/carboplatin, anthracycline/cyclophosphamide, surgery and assigned postoperative immune treatment/placebo, with no dose or appointment schedule supplied.
Pembrolizumab/placebo assignment spans preoperative and postoperative phases with no separate postoperative randomization; the whole strategy comparison cannot isolate the postoperative component.
Planned regimen components do not establish delivery to any individual patient, and a strategy illustration does not prove phase-specific benefit.
BCL-2-family death-promoting and survival roles relate to mitochondrial outer-membrane permeabilization: BAX or BAK can support the schematic pore; an obligatory mixed ring is not claimed.

BH3-only proteins have distinct activating or restraint-relieving roles, and survival proteins restrain partners rather than mechanically plugging a completed pore; no all-proteins-directly-activate rule is claimed.

Cytochrome c is shown on the intermembrane-space/crista side of the inner boundary, released through the outer membrane into cytosol, not originating in the matrix or crossing the inner membrane in this schematic.

The matrix lies inside the inner boundary and folded lumens connect to the intermembrane compartment; a local simplified patch is not exact whole-organelle morphology, pore stoichiometry or a claim that inner morphology never changes.

The spatial inset supplements rather than replaces extrinsic and intrinsic caspase routes and their BID cross-link; expression is not dependence, apoptosis is not automatic immunogenicity, and no clinical efficacy ranking follows.
Danger-signal measurements, compatible-host adaptive learning and functional protection are separate claims; DAMPs are not tumour antigens or proof of distant clinical benefit.
The described model removes the inducing chemical and uses no separate immune adjuvant before vaccinating a compatible immune-competent host; it supplies no dosing or handling protocol.

Compare vaccinated and unvaccinated hosts under matched later living same-tumour challenges, with an unrelated compatible tumour challenge for specificity; incidence and growth are functional readouts, with no assumed protection.

Severe accidental injury, regulated RIPK3/MLKL necroptosis, and apoptosis followed by inadequate clearance can converge on membrane compromise; late broken-boundary appearance or dye entry does not identify the cause.
Necrosis is broader than necroptosis, and late membrane loss can conceal an earlier apoptotic phase. The independently labelled histories do not impose one universal timeline.
Membrane loss and inflammation do not establish vaccination, whole-tumour clearance or clinical benefit; the physical boundary is observation, not mechanistic proof.
Durable division arrest in living cells differs from death, continuing metabolism and the separately testable effects of secretions; low proliferation or p21 alone is insufficient.
Secretory composition and neighbour effects depend on context; the schematic assumes no fixed SASP mixture, universal permanent arrest or inevitable relapse.
Senescence is not synonymous with ageing, quiescence or T-cell exhaustion and provides no universal marker cutoff or treatment-selection rule.
